walkthrough:
Factorise the difference of fourth powers on the left-hand side:
$$\cos^4\theta - \sin^4\theta = (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)$$

Apply the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$ and double-angle identity $\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos(2\theta)$:
$$\cos^4\theta - \sin^4\theta = \cos(2\theta)(1) = \cos(2\theta)$$

hints: Use the identity from part (a) to solve the quadratic $\cos^2(2\alpha) + \cos(2\alpha) - 1 = 0$ for $0^\circ \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the given equation to set it equal to zero:
$$\cos^4\alpha - \sin^4\alpha - 4\sin^2\alpha\cos^2\alpha = 0$$

Use the identity established in part (a) with $\theta = \alpha$:
$$\cos^2(2\alpha) + \cos(2\alpha) - 1 = 0$$

Solve this quadratic in $\cos(2\alpha)$ using the quadratic formula:
$$\cos(2\alpha) = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 4}}{2} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$$

Given $0^\circ \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 180^\circ$, the interval for $2\alpha$ is $0^\circ \leqslant 2\alpha \leqslant 360^\circ$:
- Quadrant I:
  $$2\alpha_1 = 51.827^\circ \implies \alpha_1 \approx 25.91^\circ \approx 25.9^\circ$$
- Quadrant IV:
  $$2\alpha_2 = 360^\circ - 51.827^\circ = 308.173^\circ \implies \alpha_2 \approx 154.09^\circ \approx 154.1^\circ$$

State the solutions rounded to 1 decimal place:
$$\alpha = 25.9^\circ, 154.1^\circ$$
